todo_line: - [ ] 005 Wire one-click Request access on the ordinary non-member placeholder with single-submit sending and concise sent feedback; remove the helper and Admin email only from that placeholder and sent state; preserve the access barrier and Admin contact elsewhere; and update the two authorised existing placeholder assertions.
outcome: Let an active club member outside a custom group send the accepted fixed Admin request from that group's private placeholder, with one-click sending and local sent feedback, while preserving all private-data barriers and the separate built-in Admin contact placeholder.
scope: Add an idle/sending/sent request-access interaction to the existing ordinary-non-member custom-group placeholder. The idle state has one `Request access` action, LiveView's submit state disables it with concise sending copy, and accepted message dispatch replaces it with an accessible `Your request has been sent.` status plus an explicit `Send another request` action.

Handle the request in `MemberDashboardLive` by generating a fresh typed message ID and calling `Messaging.request_group_access/2` with only the selected club ID, authenticated current person's ID, and selected group ID from socket assigns. Treat both ordinary successful return shapes as accepted-for-send; use existing generic error feedback for a rejected/failed dispatch and leave a safe retry path.

Keep the private-group title and privacy barrier copy, but remove the superseded `Think you should be? Ask the club admins.` helper and Admin mailto line from the custom-group request and sent states. Keep the existing Admin email guidance for a non-member viewing the built-in Admin Group, where Request access must not be offered.

Add focused routed LiveView coverage for eligibility, server-owned dispatch facts, single-submit/sent/repeat states, failure safety, and continued non-disclosure/non-membership. Prove request acceptance does not expose conversations, members, group email, a composer, or add the requester.

Update only the superseded Board-placeholder assertion in `acceptance-tests/features/group_conversations.feature` and `acceptance-tests/features/journeys/custom_group_admission.feature`, plus the exact domain/browser step plumbing those changed assertions require. Add `@iteration-066` to each altered scenario while retaining its existing provenance and journey selection.
scope_exclusions: Do not change the accepted `RequestGroupAccess` command/API, authoritative Membership resolver, fixed subject/body/recipient construction, email renderer, general web composition policy, or ordinary Admin conversation behavior.

Do not add a request entity, pending/approved state, deduplication, editable composer, client-supplied sender/destination/subject/body, provider-delivery claim, automatic group membership, new conversation access, or follow rights.

Do not offer Request access for built-in Everyone or Admin groups. Do not remove or alter the existing Admin Group contact assertion or its mailto behavior; only custom-group ordinary-non-member placeholders lose that alternative contact line.
Do not add the `/groups/:group_id/members/add/:person_id` route, targeted person presentation, explicit Add interaction, welcome behavior, or any task-006/007 behavior.
Do not implement or enable `acceptance-tests/features/journeys/custom_group_access_request.feature`; its `@todo` browser journey and dedicated step plumbing remain task 008.

Do not edit other acceptance scenarios, acceptance criteria, iteration planning files, ADRs, or project reference docs. Do not weaken existing name/privacy/non-joining assertions in either authorised regression scenario.
Do not run `dev check`, `dev check --quick`, `dev ci`, or another unscoped full-suite command in this packet.

references.facts: This LiveView already owns selected-group interaction state and has authoritative `selected_club`, `selected_group`, `selected_group_access`, and `current_member.id` assigns. Picker state is initialized and reset across route changes here; request UI state should likewise not leak to another selected group.

The ordinary non-member branch currently preserves privacy but uses one placeholder for both custom and built-in groups. Its first copy block is the access barrier; the later `Think you should be?` helper and Admin mailto are the superseded custom-group copy. Add stable IDs and semantic status markup for the new interaction.

An ordinary outsider receives `selected_group_access: :ordinary_non_member`, empty message/member rows, and no member count or group address. Existing code distinguishes custom groups with `SystemGroups.custom_group?/1`; request eligibility must combine custom-group identity with ordinary non-member access without broadening loaded data.

The accepted application service expects `message_id`, `club_id`, `requester_person_id`, and `group_id`, reauthorizes at a stable checkpoint, derives every message fact server-side, rejects built-in/cross-club/inactive/already-member targets, and returns the existing send dispatch result.

symbols: canonical group routes resolve same-club group identity without private rows
references.facts: This routed test currently proves the custom-group outsider's title, Admin email placeholder, absent private rows, and malformed-route privacy. Evolve the superseded custom-group contact assertion and add interaction tests here while retaining every privacy assertion.

Alice can find Board but cannot read its discussions
references.facts: Only the Board scenario's Admin-email expectation is superseded; retain its name, privacy and no-membership assertions, retain `@iteration-061`, add `@iteration-066`, and leave the separate Admin Group contact scenario unchanged and runnable.

The domain runner's current Board placeholder step asserts the old Admin address from presentation assigns. Replace only the changed Board assertion plumbing with a request-eligibility/presentation assertion; preserve the distinct generic Admin-email step.

symbols: Eve returns to Board after Dan admits her
references.facts: This already-running journey currently expects Eve's Board placeholder to show the Admin email. Change only that expectation to the approved Request access affordance, add `@iteration-066` provenance without removing `@journey`, and retain every creation, privacy, admission, non-joining, and post-admission assertion.

The browser step for Board name plus Admin email is the focused seam for the authorised journey assertion update. Keep the generic privacy step and group selection behavior intact; do not add the future iteration-066 request journey here beyond what the changed existing assertion needs.

Approved states use `Request access`, disabled `Sending your request…`, `Your request has been sent.`, and `Send another request`; sent copy says the admins have the message, the requester is not in the group yet, and a normal welcome email follows only if added.
The custom-group placeholder has no composer or alternative email contact, uses concise sending/sent feedback, and makes no tracked-status or provider-delivery promise.
Keep the routed LiveView as interaction coordinator, use stable DOM IDs and semantic status markup, and test through those IDs and public route behavior.
Use LiveView event/form conventions and selector-based tests; `phx-disable-with` is the existing project mechanism for immediate single-submit feedback.

constraints: Eligibility is server-owned: show and handle the action only when the selected group is a custom group, the current active club member has `:ordinary_non_member` access, and the local request state is idle. Recheck through `Messaging.request_group_access/2`; never trust event params for identity, club, group, destination, subject, or body, and make forged/repeated direct events outside idle a no-op.

Generate a fresh `Memba.ID.generate(:message)` for each deliberate request dispatch. Client-side disabling prevents accidental rapid resubmission, while `Send another request` deliberately returns to idle and permits a new ordinary message; do not persist or infer a pending request.

Accepted/sent means the ordinary message command was accepted, not that provider email delivery occurred or membership was granted. The sent state must continue to state or demonstrate that the requester is outside the target group.

Use one local placeholder status region with stable IDs and `role="status"` or equivalent accessible live semantics. Preserve a usable action after an error and use existing generic error presentation rather than inventing request-specific infrastructure.
Keep the custom-group privacy barrier intact: no member count, member list, group email address, conversation subject/body, tabs, New message action, or composer may appear before admission.

When the selected group is built-in Admin, retain the existing helper/Admin mailto contact and do not render a Request access action. Existing Admin rights for a requester must not be removed or contradicted.
Keep styling aligned with the existing `.access` panel, shared button component, design tokens, and responsive layout. Add only narrowly necessary styles and no new component system or inline script.

The two feature edits are assertion migrations, not scenario rewrites. Preserve all old privacy/non-joining coverage and tags, add iteration-066 provenance, and do not apply `@todo` to either already-running scenario.
Do not use `Process.sleep/1`; synchronize through strong command consistency, projections, or existing test helpers.

completion_evidence_required: Return every changed path and identify the LiveView event/state boundary and exact server-owned arguments passed to `Messaging.request_group_access/2`.
Show focused tests for custom-group outsider eligibility, disabled sending copy, accepted local status, deliberate repeat request with a fresh message, and safe generic failure/retry behavior.

Show that an accepted request creates the ordinary Admin message while leaving the requester outside the group and exposing no conversations, member rows, group email, compose surface, request record, or provider-delivery claim.
Show that forged event attributes cannot change requester, club, group, destination, subject, or body, and that built-in Admin retains its mailto guidance without a Request access action.

Identify the exact two existing feature assertions changed, confirm both retain their original privacy/non-joining semantics and gain `@iteration-066`, and confirm the future `custom_group_access_request.feature` remains `@todo` and unchanged.
Record each focused validation command, working directory, exit status, and scenario/test/failure counts; list any unresolved issue.
